Weekly Car Industry Highlights: Honda Elevate Details, Range Rover Velar Launch, and Major Recalls

Major Automotive Updates of the Week

The automotive industry witnessed several key developments, ranging from upcoming SUV announcements and luxury launches to significant safety recalls. Here is a summary of the reported highlights from the sector.

Key Industry Highlights

  • Honda Elevate Updates: Ahead of its upcoming price announcement, Honda revealed additional details regarding the compact SUV, including manufacturer-claimed fuel economy figures, as well as expected production and launch timelines.
  • Range Rover Velar Facelift: Land Rover announced prices for the facelifted Range Rover Velar in India shortly after opening order books. The luxury SUV is offered in a single, highly-equipped variant with a choice of petrol and diesel engines, featuring All-Wheel Drive (AWD) as standard.
  • Maruti-Toyota Partnership Expansion: Reports indicate that the Maruti-Toyota shared model lineup is set to expand to include a rebadged version of the Fronx crossover SUV, following the pattern of models like the Baleno and Glanza.
  • Kia Seltos Powertrain Options: The updated Kia Seltos retains its 1.5-litre naturally-aspirated and diesel engines while introducing a new 1.5-litre turbo-petrol engine option. Fuel efficiency figures reported are manufacturer claims.
  • Maruti Suzuki Safety Recall: Maruti Suzuki issued a recall affecting over 87,000 units of specific entry-level models due to a potential defect concerning the steering tie rod component.
  • Tata SUV Spyshots: Prototypes of the facelifted Tata Nexon and Tata Safari SUVs were spotted undergoing road tests, with recent spy shots revealing interior details of the updated Safari.

Other Notable Mentions

  • BYD Investment Proposal: A reported proposal by China-based EV manufacturer BYD to invest US$ 1 billion in India for local manufacturing, in partnership with a Hyderabad-based firm, was reportedly rejected by the government.
  • Toyota Innova Crysta Ambulance Conversion: Options were highlighted for converting the Toyota Innova Crysta MPV into an ambulance, featuring a full-length patient bed and medical equipment such as oxygen cylinders and monitors.
  • Mercedes-Benz V-Class Unveiling: Mercedes-Benz globally debuted a refreshed range of its V-Class luxury vans, featuring exterior design updates and a more technology-focused cabin.

Verification and Consumer Guidance

Consumers looking to verify vehicle specifications, official pricing, launch dates, or recall eligibility are advised to consult official manufacturer websites or authorized brand dealerships. Mileage or range figures mentioned in initial announcements are manufacturer-claimed specifications and may vary under real-world driving conditions.
